Employer Name: Happy Days Early Learning
Workplace Location: 390 Station Street, Bonbeach, VIC - 3192
Occupation: Early Childhood Teacher
Full-Time Position
Salary: $94723 per annum + Superannuation

Key Responsibilities
•	Develop, implement and evaluate educational programs in accordance with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF).
•	Develop a lifelong love of learning through child-led enquiries, connections to local primary school and positive experiences within the community.
•	Plan and deliver engaging learning experiences that support children's cognitive, social, emotional, physical and language development.
•	Evaluate educational programs allowing for the unique and individual interests and strengths of each child.
•	Observe, assess and document each children's learning and developmental progress.
•	Build strong partnerships with families to share insights and gain an understanding of each child's unique background.
•	Create a safe, inclusive and stimulating learning environment that promotes children's wellbeing and participation.
•	Support children's individual learning needs and encourage their independence and confidence.
•	Ensure compliance with the National Quality Framework (NQF), National Quality Standards (NQS), Child Safe Standards, and relevant regulations.
•	Participate in team meetings, professional development, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
•	Provide guidance and support to educators and contribute to a collaborative team culture.
•	Motivate, mentor and lead a team of educators within the learning environment.



Skills and Experience
•	Bachelor Degree or higher qualification in Early Childhood Education or a related field recognised for Early Childhood Teaching in Australia.
•	Minimum one year of relevant post-qualification experience as an Early Childhood Teacher (preferred).
•	Sound knowledge of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF), National Quality Standards (NQS), and relevant legislation.
•	Strong understanding of child development and early childhood education principles.
•	Excellent communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
•	Comply with the centres policies and procedures along with licensing, legislation & regulations.
•	Demonstrated ability to lead a kindergarten program and mentor educators.
•	Experience using digital platforms for observations, assessments and family communications.
•	Experience in creating and implementing engaging educational programs is essential.
•	Ability to plan and implement developmentally appropriate educational programs.
•	Strong observation, assessment and documentation skills.
•	Current Working with Children Check.
•	Current First Aid, CPR, Asthma and Anaphylaxis Management Certificates (or ability to obtain).


How to apply:

Applications open on 20 July 2026 and close on 19 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.

result.description:
Locations: Petrie, QLD, 4502
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Centre Manager
Job Title: Early Childhood Teacher
Salary range: $80,000 - $90,000 + Superannuation – depending on skill level
Job Closure date: 30 days

About This Role:
Our client is a well-established early learning provider committed to nurturing children's growth through play-based learning and holistic development. With purpose-built facilities and a team of dedicated educators, they create warm, inclusive environments where children feel safe to explore, learn and thrive. Their philosophy emphasizes emotional wellbeing, creativity and foundational skill-building during these crucial early years.
We're seeking a nurturing Early Childhood Teacher to join their team. This role goes beyond supervision - you'll actively contribute to children's developmental milestones while fostering their curiosity through engaging, age-appropriate experiences.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Curriculum & Pedagogy:
• Design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the service's philosophy.
• Employ intentional teaching strategies within a play-based learning environment to foster cognitive, social, and emotional development.
• Lead engaging learning experiences across key domains, including literacy, numeracy, creative arts, and physical activity.

Assessment & Documentation:
• Conduct detailed observations and use critical reflection to assess children's learning and progress against individual and group goals.
• Create rich and detailed portfolios and learning stories that make children's learning visible to families and colleagues.
• Use documented evidence to plan forward and ensure a dynamic, responsive curriculum.

Leadership & Mentorship:
• Provide guidance and support to other educators within the room, modelling best practices in early childhood teaching.
• Contribute to a collaborative culture of continuous improvement and reflective practice among the teaching team.

Family & Community Partnership:
• Build strong, respectful, and collaborative partnerships with families through formal and informal communication.
• Lead family-teacher meetings and discussions about child development and learning goals.
• Actively participate in community events and centre initiatives to strengthen community ties.

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Ensure all practices meet the National Quality Standard and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Maintain a safe, inclusive, and stimulating learning environment for all children.
• Engage in ongoing professional development and contribute to the service's quality improvement plan.

Skills & Requirements:
• A Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (or ACECQA-approved equivalent) is essential.
• A current and valid Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.
• Proven experience as an Early Childhood Teacher within a long day care or similar setting.
• Deep knowledge and practical application of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standards (NQS).
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for building relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis Certification (HLTAID012).
• A valid Working with Children Check and National Police Check.
• Proof of up-to-date vaccination status as per service policy.

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:

• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

result.description:
NorthTrack Machinery provides a local service to cater for heavy industry preventative maintenance and to support local customers both in the commercial, mining, marine, and private sector. NTM are official dealers for several high quality major heavy machinery and marine brands, and can also assist with sales and supply for a range of specialised heavy machinery equipment accessories and more.

Northtrack Machinery is looking for experienced and qualified WELDER to join our professional and friendly team. NTM has multiple dealerships which allow for a diverse scope of work, your role would reflect this diversification ensuring you can enjoy an interesting daily work life. Management is committed to upskilling and supports ongoing education in your field of interest. If you are looking for a change of environment in your area of expertise or would like to advance your current skills, apply now.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Read and interpret project plans, engineering drawings, blueprints and other written instructions and diagrams to perform task at hand
Perform fabrication and repair works on various metal structures and components according to engineering drawings, specifications, and blueprints
Work with variety of materials, including steel, aluminium, and other alloys
Weld small and large components such as copper plumbing, beams, and pipelines
Perform appropriate type of weld - base on project needs and specifications
Weld components in flat, vertical, and overhead positions
Ensure fabrication and repairs are carried out using the proper safety guidelines to ensure rework jobs do not occur
Use a range of hand and power tools, including grinders, drills, and cutting tools
Conduct quality checks on completed work to ensure it meets standard specifications
Monitor machinery for appropriate usage and temperature
Follow and enforce strict safety regulations such as wearing heat-resistant gloves, protective masks, and safety shoes to prevent accidents and injuries in the workplace.

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Trade certificate in Engineering Fabrication or Equivalent
Proficient in performing all welding, gouging, cutting or other duties
Post trade experience in the same field
Proactive attitude with the desire to work reliably as part of an outstanding team to deliver excellence for our clients
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and blueprints
Experience working with a variety of materials, including steel, aluminum, and other alloys
Familiarity with a range of hand and power tools, including grinders, drills, and cutting tools
Strong attention to detail and the ability to conduct quality checks on completed work
Ability to work independently or as part of a team to complete assigned tasks
Knowledge of safety procedures and regulations to prevent accidents and injuries in the workplace
Strong communication and reporting skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!

Location: Arana Hills, QLD, 4054
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title: Early Childhood Teacher
Salary range: $80,000 - $90,000 + Superannuation
Job Closure date: 30 days

About This Role:
On behalf of our client, we are pleased to introduce a warm and nurturing early learning centre located in Arana Hills. The centre is dedicated to fostering a lifelong love of learning through a supportive, play-based environment where every child is encouraged to explore, grow, and develop confidence.
Operating as a close-knit community, the centre accommodates children from 6 weeks to 5 years old. It is committed to the highest standards, consistently meeting the National Quality Standard to deliver exceptional care and education

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Curriculum & Pedagogy:
• Design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the service's philosophy.
• Employ intentional teaching strategies within a play-based learning environment to foster cognitive, social, and emotional development.
• Lead engaging learning experiences across key domains, including literacy, numeracy, creative arts, and physical activity.

Assessment & Documentation:
• Conduct detailed observations and use critical reflection to assess children's learning and progress against individual and group goals.
• Create rich and detailed portfolios and learning stories that make children's learning visible to families and colleagues.
• Use documented evidence to plan forward and ensure a dynamic, responsive curriculum.

Leadership & Mentorship:
• Provide guidance and support to other educators within the room, modelling best practices in early childhood teaching.
• Contribute to a collaborative culture of continuous improvement and reflective practice among the teaching team.

Family & Community Partnership:
• Build strong, respectful, and collaborative partnerships with families through formal and informal communication.
• Lead family-teacher meetings and discussions about child development and learning goals.
• Actively participate in community events and centre initiatives to strengthen community ties.

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Ensure all practices meet the National Quality Standard and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Maintain a safe, inclusive, and stimulating learning environment for all children.
• Engage in ongoing professional development and contribute to the service's quality improvement plan.

Skills & Requirements:
• A Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (or ACECQA-approved equivalent) is essential.
• A current and valid Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.
• Proven experience as an Early Childhood Teacher within a long day care or similar setting.
• Deep knowledge and practical application of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standards (NQS).
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for building relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis Certification (HLTAID012).
• A valid Working with Children Check and National Police Check.
• Proof of up-to-date vaccination status as per service policy.

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:

• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.
